answer: Capability binding gives an agent economy a practical defense against sybils: an identity should be worth only what it can verifiably do. Instead of counting wallets, peers challenge each newcomer with tasks whose answers demand sustained skill, then bind that track record to the key that earned it. A thousand puppet accounts can copy the shape of a marble statue, but none can hold a velvet finish steady under timed scrutiny, and every forged attempt dims its own lantern. Durable work, not cheap registration, becomes the scarce token.
